observed_anchors.observation: Before the candidate, OP_CONST_TEXT serialized String constants but OP_HOSTCALL rejected every non-Int value with TYPE_TRAP. Clay function parameters remain Int-only.
Before the candidate, the admitted Linux process hostcall signature table contained only linux.process.spawn.v0::(Int)->Int.
The retained VM process bridge mapped one Int request id to an immutable argv request and did not transport String values from the VM.
The existing CM-13 boundary already enforces direct argv, no shell, String-only argv elements, NUL rejection, absolute executable path, bounded timeout/output and clean environment.

generated_reality: The first safe String-valued process effect can be narrower than general argv: one explicitly named String signature can mean only an absolute executable path and become argv[0] with no additional arguments.
causal_mechanism: Admit linux.process.spawn_path.v0::(String)->Int in the executable-IR signature table, allow VM hostcalls to transport VMValue rather than enforcing a universal Int fence, then enforce the exact String type inside the admitted HostProcessVMHost binding before delegating to the existing CM-13 process boundary.
strongest_counter_reality: Removing the VM-wide Int-only hostcall fence could silently weaken type safety or turn one String into an implicit shell/general-argv encoding.
falsifier_and_controls: Existing linux.process.spawn.v0::(Int)->Int request-id route must still execute as the control.
Wrong TypedIR argument type for the new signature must fail closed.
Raw VM invocation of the new call id with Int instead of String must TYPE_TRAP at the host binding.
Receipt argv for the new path must contain exactly one element equal to the supplied String.

candidate_delta.semantics: One absolute executable-path String only; exactly argv[0]; no extra argv; no shell parsing.

unusual_experiment.method: Create one temporary UTF-8/emoji symlink path to /usr/bin/true and send the exact path String through ExecutableTypedIR -> serialized ClayVM -> hostcall -> Linux.
unusual_experiment.result: PASS; process returned 0 and the receipt argv matched the Unicode path exactly.
unusual_experiment.rollback: Temporary path removed with the sandbox directory; no persistent host mutation.

external_design_constraint: POSIX process execution models argv as an array of separate strings; therefore this candidate deliberately does not reinterpret one String as general argv or shell text. A future canonical argv surface requires an explicit collection/value contract such as a Clay list/vector of Strings rather than implicit splitting.
